title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [July 27 - Aug 01]
summary:
This week, 17 Indian startups raised nearly $82.2 million across 2 growth stage deals, 13 early stage deals, and 2 undisclosed deals. The week also witnessed 8 key hires, 4 fund launches, 1 M&A deal, and 1 ESOP buyback.

In contrast, 16 startups had collectively secured about $164 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised a total of $21.1 million across two deals this week, led by Apna Mart, which raised Rs 120 crore (around $12.7 million) in its Series C round co-led by Accel India and Fundamentum, with participation from Peak XV Partners.
Hyderabad-based dairy brand Sid’s Farm followed with over Rs 81 crore (around $8.4 million) in a pre-Series B round led by Omnivore, NSFO, Dodla Dairy, Next Bharat Ventures, and LIO.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $61.1 million across 13 deals this week, led by Arboreal Bioinnovations, which secured Rs 230 crore (over $24 million) in a Series A round co-led by EAAA and Omnivore. 
Aham Housing Finance followed with Rs 100 crore in a follow-on funding round led by The Sanmar Group, while Omega Seiki Mobility raised Rs 50 crore from Securocorp Securities, Sangeeta Pareekh, Saket Aggarwal Family Office, and Vanshika Sharma.
Among the other notable deals, healthtech startup Fixxly, Bengaluru-based AI startup Revspot, agriculture drone startup SUIND, global student living technology company House of Student, and six other early-stage startups also raised funds this week.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru continued to lead the funding charts with 7 startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR with five deals. Mumbai, Hyderabad and Chennai also recorded deals.

Segment-wise, fintech, edtech, e-commerce startups led the week with two deals each. Foodtech, FMCG, dairy tech, EV, Proptech, AI and others also bagged deals during the week. 
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with 7 deals, followed by 6 Series A deals. Series C, and pre- Series B rounds also witnessed activity during the week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding declined 50% to $82.2 million, compared to around $164 million raised during the previous week.
The average funding over the last eight weeks stands at around $316 million, with an average of 21 deals per week.
[Key Hirings]
This week, Instamart appointed former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha as its Chief Executive Officer, while Nykaa named former Instamart COO Ankit Jain to lead its quick commerce arm, Nykaa Now. JITO Incubation and Innovation Foundation (JIIF) appointed Anshu Jain as its Chief Operating Officer, and Neo Group named Anirban Banerjee as Co-founder and Chief People and Transformation Officer. Separately, a company appointed Subhasis Chaudhuri, Suman Gopalan, and Anand Vora as independent directors.
[Fund Launches]
This week, Cactus Partners announced its second fund with a target corpus of Rs 1,600 crore, while Inflexor Ventures marked the first close of its third fund at Rs 400 crore against a target of Rs 1,250 crore. Anicut Capital launched a Rs 250 crore seed fund for early-stage startups, and Groww’s co-founders are planning a second fund with a target corpus of Rs 400 crore to Rs 500 crore.

title: UPI hits highest ever monthly volume with 23.66 Bn transactions in July
summary:
Unified Payments Interface (UPI) recorded its highest ever monthly transaction volume in July 2026, with 23.66 billion transactions worth Rs 29.88 lakh crore, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The July numbers surpassed the previous record of 23.20 billion transactions set in May this year. However, transaction value remained marginally below the all time high of Rs 29.90 lakh crore recorded in the same month.
On a daily basis, UPI processed 763 million transactions, while the average daily transaction value stood at Rs 96,383 crore.
Compared to June, transaction volume increased 4.1% from 22.72 billion, while transaction value rose 3.3% from Rs 28.92 lakh crore. On a year on year basis, transaction volume grew 22%, while transaction value increased 19%.
UPI crossed the 23 billion monthly transaction mark for the first time in May.
As of June, Walmart backed digital payments platform PhonePe retained its lead in the UPI ecosystem with 10.48 billion transactions, followed by Google Pay and Paytm in the second and third spots, respectively. Meanwhile, WhatsApp surpassed CRED in UPI transaction volume, processing 150.48 million transactions compared with 141.78 million for CRED. NPCI is yet to release the app wise transaction data for July.
Recently, the Maldives launched a real time payment corridor with India, further expanding UPI's global footprint. UPI merchant payments are now live in 10 international markets: Bhutan, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Qatar, Cambodia, and the Maldives. Greece remains connected for person to person transfers, while Singapore and Nepal also support remittance linkages.

title: TVS extends lead in July as Ola Electric, Ather record decline in EV two-wheeler sales
summary:
EV two-wheeler registrations in India stayed above 1.93 lakh in July 2026. TVS Motor strengthened its leadership by crossing 50,000 registrations, while Ola Electric and Ather Energy witnessed a drop in sales.
According to the latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the EV two-wheeler market with 52,538 registrations in July and a 27.15% market share. The company posted 10.8% month-on-month growth, with 5,125 more registrations than in June.
Bajaj Auto retained the second spot with 43,607 registrations and a 22.53% market share in July. Its registrations rose marginally from 43,504 units in June.
Ather Energy retained the third position with 28,819 registrations and a 14.89% market share in July. The company recorded an 8.3% month-on-month decline, with 2,616 fewer registrations than in June.
Hero MotoCorp ranked fourth with 21,174 registrations and a 10.94% market share in July. The company reported a marginal 3.3% month-on-month decline. 
Ola Electric remained fifth with 13,170 registrations and a 6.80% market share in July. The company recorded one of the steepest declines among the leading EV two-wheeler makers, with sales falling 19% month on month, or by 3,079 units, from 16,249 registrations in July.
Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 9,701 registrations and a 5.01% market share after its sales dropped 11.3% over June.
Among the fastest-growing players in the top 10, BGauss recorded the strongest month-on-month growth at 33.9%, with registrations rising to 5,324 units. River Mobility followed with a 24.8% increase to 5,554 units.
Among the other players, Simple Energy posted an 11.2% month-on-month growth, with registrations rising to 1,532 units in July. Lectrix EV entered the top 10 after its registrations increased 22.8% over June to 1,335 units.

title: InstaHelp earns Rs 29 per order while losing Rs 346 in Q1 FY27
summary:
Urban Company’s quick home services platform InstaHelp recorded an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 346 per order in Q1 FY27, an improvement from Rs 447 per order in Q4 FY26, even as its overall losses widened during the quarter.
InstaHelp’s adjusted EBITDA loss stood at Rs 132 crore in Q1 FY27 as compared to Rs 119 crore in the preceding quarter. The platform fulfilled 3.82 million orders during the quarter, up 43% from 2.67 million orders in Q4 FY26.
The platform generated Rs 11.22 crore in revenue during the quarter, up from Rs 9 crore in Q4 FY26. Its net transaction value (NTV) increased 32% quarter on quarter to Rs 52.9 crore from Rs 40.1 crore.
Launched in March 2025, InstaHelp’s NTV has grown steadily since its launch, increasing from Rs 27.6 crore in Q3 FY26 to Rs 40.1 crore in Q4 FY26 and Rs 52.9 crore in Q1 FY27. Fulfilled orders also increased from 1.6 million in Q3 FY26 to 2.67 million in Q4 FY26 and 3.82 million in Q1 FY27.
At the same time, average order value declined to Rs 138 in Q1 FY27 from Rs 150 in the previous quarter amid competitive pricing in the segment. Based on its operating revenue and fulfilled orders, InstaHelp’s revenue per order also declined to around Rs 29.4 from Rs 33.3 in the preceding quarter.
Despite the increase in absolute losses, InstaHelp’s loss per order declined nearly 23% quarter on quarter to Rs 346 from Rs 447. Urban Company attributed the improvement to higher network density as order volumes scaled. In Q3 FY26, the platform’s adjusted EBITDA loss per order stood at Rs 381.
“In this phase of category development, we are prioritising market leadership over everything else,” Urban Company said in its shareholder letter.
The company expects margins to remain under pressure in the near term as aggressive discounting continues across the market. Urban Company said current pricing levels are unsustainable for the industry and that pricing normalisation could lead to a one-time adjustment in demand across the category.
Competition in the quick home services segment has also intensified. According to Moneycontrol, Snabbit recorded 1.51 million orders in June, while Urban Company’s InstaHelp clocked around 1.5 million orders during the month. Pronto recorded around 0.95 million orders during the same period.

title: Urban Company posts 92 Cr loss on Rs 528 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27
summary:
Home services marketplace Urban Company reported a strong 44% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in Q1 FY27. However, the company slipped into a loss of Rs 92 crore during the quarter amid its continued push for InstaHelp.
According to the company’s quarterly financial results, Urban Company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 528 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 367 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The India Consumer Services business, excluding InstaHelp, remained Urban Company's largest revenue contributor, accounting for more than 67% of its operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew 31% year-on-year to Rs 356 crore during the quarter.
The company's Native brands business recorded a 58% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 95 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 60 crore in the year-ago period, while its international business grew 81% to contribute Rs 65 crore.
Meanwhile, InstaHelp, Urban Company's quick-service housekeeping vertical launched in March last year, generated Rs 11.11 crore in revenue during the quarter. However, the segment reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 131.58 crore, up 11% sequentially from Rs 118.73 crore in Q4 FY26.
The company also earned Rs 38 crore from non-operating sources during the quarter, taking its overall income to Rs 566 crore. On a quarterly basis, overall revenue grew by 23% from Rs 462 crore in Q4 FY26.
On the expense side, Urban Company's employee benefit expenses rose 53% year-on-year to Rs 151 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 99 crore in the same quarter last year, while its cost of materials increased 45% to Rs 100 crore.
Finance costs, depreciation and amortisation expenses, along with other undisclosed costs, pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 640 crore during the quarter from Rs 384 crore in Q1 FY26.
Despite strong revenue growth, Urban Company slipped to a loss of Rs 92 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a profit of Rs 7 crore in the year-ago quarter, as it continued to make significant investments in its quick-service housekeeping vertical, InstaHelp.
At the end of Friday’s trading session, Urban Company’s shares closed 6% lower at Rs 129.39 compared to the previous closing price, taking the company’s total market capitalization to Rs 19,894 crore ($2.1 billion).

title: Shadowfax clocks Rs 1,358 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27, profit rises over 8X
summary:
Shadowfax Technologies reported a strong performance in Q1 FY27, with the logistics and last-mile delivery firm recording a 65% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. Its profit also surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore during the quarter.
The company’s revenue from operations surged to Rs 1,358 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 824 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from NSE.


 
Shadowfax operates in the last-mile and hyperlocal logistics segment, catering to ecommerce marketplaces, D2C brands, and quick commerce platforms. The company competes with Delhivery, XpressBees, Ecom Express, and Ekart in a highly competitive market.
The company also recorded Rs 21 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,379 crore in Q1 FY27. On a sequential basis, total income grew 10% from Rs 1,253 crore reported in Q4 FY26.
The company did not disclose a detailed expense breakup. Its employee benefit expenses rose 49% year-on-year to Rs 124 crore, while depreciation and amortisation costs increased 82% to Rs 40 crore. Overall, Shadowfax's total expenditure grew 60% year-on-year to Rs 1,314 crore during the quarter.
Shadowfax Technologies' profit surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 8 crore in the year-ago quarter, as the company's revenue growth continued to outpace the increase in its expenses.
As of 12:41 PM today, Shadowfax's share price was up 8% at around Rs 237, valuing the company at Rs 13,848 crore (approximately $1.45 billion).

As per an Economic Times report, Atomberg's engineering arm is in talks to raise Rs 150–200 crore in a funding round led by General Catalyst at a valuation of Rs 1,500–1,700 crore. The report added that the company is targeting a Rs 2,000 crore IPO, with Avendus and IIFL Capital appointed as bankers for the proposed issue.
Atomberg is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, the Mumbai-based company crossed the Rs 1,000 crore total income mark, with operating revenue rising 20% to Rs 958.4 crore from Rs 796.9 crore in FY24. The Temasek-backed firm also narrowed its net loss by 41% to Rs 117.4 crore

title: Swiggy Q1 FY27 revenue jumps 37% to Rs 6,812 Cr, loss narrows 34%
summary:
Foodtech and quick commerce major Swiggy reported a 37% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue to Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4,961 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company also narrowed its losses by 34% during the period.
Scootsy Logistics, Swiggy’s supply chain and distribution arm, remained its largest revenue contributor, accounting for nearly 47% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from the segment rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 3,195 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,259 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Swiggy’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses also posted strong growth during the quarter. Revenue from food delivery increased 23% year-on-year to Rs 2,208 crore, while quick commerce arm Instamart recorded a 53% jump to Rs 1,232 crore.

The remaining operating revenue came from segments such as dine-out services and other initiatives, including Bolt and Toing.
The company also reported Rs 211 crore in other income. As a result, its total income rose to Rs 7,023 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 5,048 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On the expense front, procurement of materials remained Swiggy's largest cost centre at Rs 2,975 crore during the quarter. Employee benefit expenses declined marginally by 3.5% to Rs 662 crore. Advertising and sales promotion expenses stood at Rs 1,160 crore, while delivery costs amounted to Rs 1,750 crore. Other operational expenses pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 7,813 crore in Q1 FY27.
Segment-wise, Swiggy's food delivery business remained EBITDA positive with an EBITDA of Rs 299 crore, while its quick commerce arm, Instamart, continued to incur losses and reported a negative EBITDA of Rs 651 crore during the quarter.

Swiggy's losses narrowed 34% year-on-year to Rs 791 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,197 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, aided by strong revenue growth.

On a sequential basis, the company's losses remained largely flat at Rs 791 crore compared with Rs 799 crore in Q4 FY26, while revenue grew 7% from Rs 6,383 crore.

Swiggy’s shares closed at Rs 295.91 on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 81,098 crore ($8.53 billion). 

On the competitive front, rival Eternal reported a profit of Rs 92 crore on an operating revenue of Rs 20,211 crore in Q1 FY27.

title: PhonePe launches PulsePro for enterprise market intelligence
summary:
Fullstack fintech platform PhonePe has launched PulsePro, an enterprise intelligence platform that provides businesses with market insights based on aggregated and anonymised transaction data from its payments network.
PulsePro enables enterprises to analyse consumer spending trends, category performance and local market dynamics for decisions related to expansion planning, distribution strategy, site selection and category growth. According to PhonePe, the platform offers near real time insights derived from transaction data, addressing the limitations of traditional survey based market research.
The company also shared a set of hyperlocal consumer insights generated through PulsePro. According to PhonePe, Chakan in Pune recorded the highest number of OTT users in the country, while Maharashtra led in pet related spending. Kurung Kumey district in Arunachal Pradesh reported lifestyle spending at nearly three times the state average. Jabalpur emerged as the top healthcare spending district in Madhya Pradesh, while Marathahalli in Bengaluru recorded the highest number of late night orders nationwide.
PulsePro is built on PhonePe’s payments ecosystem, which spans more than 700 million registered users, over 50 million registered merchants and 99% of India’s postal codes. It extends PhonePe Pulse, the company’s public data platform launched in 2021 for entrepreneurs, researchers, developers, policymakers and students.
While PhonePe Pulse will continue to remain free, PulsePro is positioned as a paid enterprise offering with advanced market intelligence capabilities.
The platform covers more than 200 store categories and over 100 market signals, enabling businesses to analyse spending patterns, identify growth opportunities and evaluate changes in consumer behaviour.
PulsePro also provides district and postal code level insights to support distribution planning, urban expansion, rural market prioritisation and site selection. In addition, it tracks digital commerce indicators, including quick commerce penetration at a hyperlocal level.
“Businesses today don’t just need more data, they need better intelligence. Since launching PhonePe Pulse in 2021, we have seen a growing demand from organizations looking for deeper market insights to guide expansion and strategic decision making. PhonePe PulsePro is our response to that need,” said Karthik Raghupathy, Head of Strategy at PhonePe.
According to PhonePe, PulsePro generates enterprise insights using aggregated and anonymised transaction trends while maintaining user privacy.

title: InCred Finance reports Rs 759 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps 83%
summary:
InCred Financial Services, the lending arm of InCred Holdings, carried its growth momentum into FY27 after reporting a strong financial performance in FY26. The company posted a 31% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue, while profit surged 83% to Rs 172 crore in Q1 FY27.
According to its standalone financial statements sourced from BSE, the Mumbai-based company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 759 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 580 crore in Q1 FY26.

Founded in 2017 by Bhupinder Singh, InCred Finance is a retail-focused NBFC that provides personal loans, education loans, secured business loans, MSME financing, and lending solutions for financial institutions.
Interest income remained the company's largest revenue driver, contributing nearly 90% of its operating revenue. Revenue from this segment rose to Rs 682 crore in Q1 FY27. Fee and commission income added Rs 67 crore, while the rest came from gains on fair value changes in financial assets.
Including Rs 3 crore from non-operating income, InCred Finance's total income stood at Rs 762 crore during the quarter.
InCred Finance's loan book (excluding assigned loans) grew to Rs 14,809 crore at the end of June 2026, driven by continued momentum across its five lending verticals. The company also reported an improvement in asset quality, with gross NPAs declining to 2.0% from 2.3% a year ago and net NPAs easing to 0.7% from 0.9%. Its net worth stood at Rs 4,244 crore as of June 30, 2026.
Finance costs remained the largest expense for InCred Finance, accounting for 51% of its total expenditure. These costs rose 26% year-on-year to Rs 270 crore in Q1 FY27. Employee benefit expenses increased 39% to Rs 131 crore during the quarter.
Losses from impaired financial instruments, including loan write-offs, declined 44% year-on-year to Rs 43 crore. Depreciation charges, along with legal, collection, advertising, travel and other overheads, pushed the company's total expenditure up 15% to Rs 533 crore from Rs 465 crore in Q1 FY26.
InCred Finance's profit surged 83% year-on-year to Rs 172 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 94 crore in the year-ago quarter.

title: Apna Mart raises Rs 120 Cr in Series C round led by Accel, Fundamentum
summary:
Franchise-led omnichannel grocery and FMCG startup Apna Mart has raised Rs 120 crore (around $12.7 million) in a Series C funding round co-led by existing investors Accel India and Fundamentum, with participation from Peak XV Partners.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the company's working capital and support its expansion across India. The transaction was advised by VERTICES PARTNERS, which acted as legal counsel to Apna Mart.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the funding round in June after accessing the company's regulatory filings.
The round valued the Gurugram-based company at around Rs 1,470 crore, nearly double its previous valuation of Rs 738 crore, as per Entrackr's estimates.
Founded by Abhishek Singh and Chetan Garg, Apna Mart operates a franchise-led omnichannel quick commerce platform focused on Tier II and Tier III cities. The startup delivers groceries through a neighborhood store-led model and competes with Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and Zepto.
The Series C round comes a little over a year after Apna Mart raised around $25 million in its Series B funding led by Accel and Fundamentum.
The company recently said its operating revenue grew 2.5X to Rs 500 crore in FY26, although it did not disclose its bottom line. In FY25, it reported operating revenue of Rs 185 crore and a net loss of Rs 76 crore.
Apna Mart also laid off around 10% of its workforce this year and shifted its headquarters from Bengaluru to Gurugram.

title: Peak XV makes another Go Digit exit, sells shares worth Rs 139 Cr via block deal
summary:
Peak XV Partners, an early investor in Go Digit General Insurance, has offloaded shares worth around Rs 139 crore through a block deal on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). This is its second stake sale in the company in less than two months.
 
According to NSE block deal data, Peak XV Partners, through its affiliate Peak XV Partners Growth Investments III, sold 57.21 lakh shares of Go Digit at Rs 243 share price taking the transaction value to approximately Rs 139 crore. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund acquired the entire tranche at the same price.
 
In June, Peak XV sold 33.33 lakh shares of Go Digit for Rs 100 crore. The transaction saw participation from Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and JPMorgan (Taiwan) Eastern Technology Fund.
 
With the latest transaction, Peak XV has sold 90.54 lakh Go Digit shares worth around Rs 239 crore across the two block deals.
 
Founded in 2017, Go Digit General Insurance offers products across motor, health, travel, property and other insurance segments. Motor insurance remains its largest business line, followed by health and fire insurance. The company counts Faering Capital, Wellington Management and TVS Capital Funds among its backers.
 
On the financial front, Go Digit’s profit after tax declined 37.5% to Rs 86.4 crore in Q1 FY27, from Rs 138.3 crore in the year-ago period. Its gross premium written also fell 8.4% to Rs 2,730.9 crore from Rs 2,981.8 crore in Q1 FY26.
 
The latest stake sale comes amid pressure on Go Digit’s stock. The insurer’s shares hit an all-time low of Rs 245 on the BSE on July 28 and have declined nearly 21% over the past month.
Go Digit’s shares were trading at Rs 252 as of 10:56 AM, taking its market capitalization to around Rs 23,430 crore.

title: Drone startup SUIND raises Rs 20.5 Cr in seed round led by Transition VC
summary:
Agriculture drone startup SUIND has raised Rs 20.5 crore ($2.2 million) in a seed funding round led by Transition VC. The round also saw participation from IIMA Ventures.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the development recently. 
The fresh capital will be used to scale the commercial deployment of its agriculture drone platform, accelerate the development of its autonomous surveillance and infrastructure inspection drone, strengthen its proprietary autonomy technology and expand its engineering team.
Founded in 2020 by Kunal Shrivastava and Kevin Kleber, SUIND develops autonomous unmanned aerial systems that use computer vision for navigation instead of relying primarily on GPS. Its technology enables drones to operate in low-altitude and GPS-denied environments.
The startup has commercially deployed its DGCA-certified autonomous spraying drone, Bumblebee, across farms and plantations. It is also developing WASP, an autonomous aerial platform for industrial monitoring, security, surveillance and defence applications.
Over the next 12 to 24 months, SUIND plans to scale the manufacturing and deployment of Bumblebee while preparing WASP for commercial launch. The agriculture drone ecosystem in India has witnessed growing interest in recent years, driven by demand for precision farming and government support for drone adoption. Suind competes with startups such as Marut Drones, Garuda Aerospace, IoTechWorld Avigation, BharatRohan, and Dhaksha Unmanned Systems.

title: Indian Physical AI attracts $155 Mn in 2026 as robotics, real-world data gain traction
summary:
Home services startup Pronto’s decision to expand its Physical AI experiment involving wearable cameras inside customers’ homes has brought the emerging technology into focus, particularly the opportunity around real-world data for training AI and robotics systems.
The move comes even as larger home services players Snabbit and Urban Company's InstaHelp have opted out of similar initiatives. Pronto, which has raised $45 million in funding this year alone, is expanding its opt-in Pronto Verified service, which records service sessions and uses anonymized footage for AI training. As companies explore ways to collect real-world data for AI and robotics, investor interest is also growing across robotics, autonomous systems, AI-powered hardware, and training infrastructure.
Year-on-year funding trend
According to data compiled by Entrackr, startups in the Indian Physical AI ecosystem have raised around $155 million across 31 deals in 2026 so far. This compares with $130 million across 25 deals in 2025, $124 million across 24 deals in 2024, and $91 million across 21 deals in 2023, according to Venture Intelligence data.

For this analysis, the funding dataset includes startups headquartered in India, as well as overseas companies with significant Physical AI product development, commercial deployment, or data collection in India. Companies with only engineering or support teams in India, or where Physical AI remains an experimental or ancillary initiative, such as Pronto, are excluded from the funding tally.
Funding in 2026 so far is already about 19% higher than the total raised in 2025 and more than 70% above 2023 levels. Most companies that raised capital this year are early-stage ventures, though capital remains concentrated among a few larger rounds. Innefu Labs, Unbox Robotics, and Deccan AI together raised $83 million, accounting for more than half of the $155 million raised so far.
Perhaps predictably, this remains the safest bet on the AI boom, in terms of predictable, if relatively tiny part of it. With firms building their own layers on top of existing frontier AI networks or otherwise. Some would say this is just as well, pointing to the havoc the rise in valuations, followed by the crash it has caused in South Korea this month.
Growth-stage deals lead the pack
Innefu Labs led the segment with a $30 million Series B round led by Panthera Growth Partners. The national security-focused AI company is also building a dedicated Physical AI and robotics division for defence and security applications.
Supply chain robotics startup Unbox Robotics raised $28 million in a round led by ICICI Venture, with participation from RedStartLabs, F Prime, 3one4 Capital, Navam Capital, Force Ventures, and existing investors.
Deccan AI raised $25 million in a Series A round led by A91 Partners, with participation from SIG and Prosus Ventures. The startup provides data and model training, post-training data, and evaluation services for frontier AI labs, and has expanded into enterprise AI solutions.
Outside the funding dataset, US-based physical security AI startup Hakimo, founded by Indian-origin entrepreneurs Sam Joseph and Sagar Honnungar, raised $12 million in a growth round led by Zigg Capital, with participation from Neotribe Ventures, Vertex Ventures, Defy.vc, and Rocketship.vc. It uses AI to automate physical security monitoring through existing camera infrastructure.
Early-stage startups gain momentum
Marine robotics company Rekise Marine raised $9.7 million in a seed round co-led by Accel and NKSquared. It builds autonomous ships and submarines and partners with Indian shipyards for vessel design and integration.
San Francisco and Bengaluru-based Human Archive raised $8.2 million in a round led by Wing Venture Capital and NVP Capital. The Y Combinator-backed company came into the spotlight in India following early talks with Snabbit around a potential Physical AI initiative, though the home services startup eventually decided not to proceed. Human Archive is building large-scale human sensorimotor datasets to train robots and Physical AI systems.
Bengaluru-based SwitchOn raised $8 million in a pre-Series B round led by IvyCap Ventures. The startup develops AI-powered vision systems for automated quality inspection across manufacturing production lines.
Other notable rounds include Spector.ai’s $6.7 million raise led by IvyCap Ventures and ANSCER Robotics’ $5.4 million (Rs 45 crore) Series A led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from Info Edge.
Bengaluru and Detroit-based Mowito raised $3 million in a pre-seed round led by Version One Ventures to build AI foundation models that enable industrial robotic arms to learn manufacturing tasks through demonstrations. Construction-focused Physical AI and robotics startup Flo Mobility raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round co-led by Mela Ventures and Arali Ventures.
The remaining funding was spread across more than 20 deeptech and robotics startups, including AutoVRse, WorkOnGrid, RoshAI, Armatrix, Constems, and others. The investor base across these deals includes mainstream venture and growth funds such as Accel, A91 Partners, ICICI Venture, IvyCap Ventures, 3one4 Capital, Prosus Ventures, SIG, Info Edge, and Version One Ventures. 
The data layer around Physical AI
A separate set of companies is working on the data collection, annotation, and training infrastructure required for Physical AI systems. Human Archive is building human sensorimotor datasets for robots and Physical AI systems, while Neocambrian AI has launched an India-focused robotics data factory. Other companies working across this layer in India include iMerit, Human Stryde, Luel, Awign, Build, Centific, Humyn Labs, Aura ML, Build AI, FPV Labs, and Northstar.
Physical AI models require real-world data that captures human actions, objects, environments, and interactions. Much of this data has to be collected specifically for robotics and embodied AI use cases rather than sourced from existing internet datasets.
Pronto offers another example of how such data could be generated. While the company is not included in the $155 million Physical AI funding tally, its experiment shows how businesses with workers operating in real-world environments could become a source of training data.
Larger rounds could follow
Skylark Labs, led by India-born founder and CEO Amarjot Singh, has a significant India presence and works with the country’s defence ecosystem, including the Indian Army, Indian Air Force, and ideaForge. The company is in talks to raise $100–150 million at a valuation of more than $1 billion.
If completed, the round would be substantially larger than any individual Physical AI funding round involving an India-linked company in 2026.
Physical AI companies, particularly those building hardware, will still have to deal with higher deployment costs and longer commercial cycles. For companies collecting real-world data, privacy and consent will remain key concerns, especially for data collected inside homes.

title: Kissht clocks Rs 670 Cr revenue and Rs 95 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
summary:
Digital lending platform Kissht reported its first quarterly results for the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company's operating revenue grew 45% year-on-year in the quarter, while its profit increased 58% to Rs 95 crore.
Kissht’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 670 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 463 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.
Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, provides small-ticket consumer loans and has scaled aggressively through partnerships with merchants across electronics, fashion, travel, and other categories. The company primarily earns interest income from these loans, although a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter was not disclosed.
The company also earned Rs 7 crore from non operating sources, raising its total revenue to Rs 677 crore.
Kissht continued to expand its lending business during the quarter, with its assets under management (AUM) growing 61% year-on-year and 13% sequentially to Rs 8,001 crore. The company has cumulatively served over 12.25 million customers, a 26% increase from a year ago. Its off-book AUM stood at Rs 4,284 crore, accounting for 53.6% of the total portfolio, reflecting its capital-light partnership model.
Impairment on financial instruments remained one of the largest expense heads for the fintech platform, accounting for over 23% of the total cost base. The expense grew 28% year on year to Rs 128 crore in Q1 FY27, while finance costs increased 39% to Rs 82 crore.
Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 71 crore, while spending on marketing, legal and professional services, and IT expenses drove the company's total expenditure up 42% year on year to Rs 549 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 386 crore in the same quarter last year.
In the end, strong revenue growth helped the Mumbai-based company post a 58% year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 95 crore in Q1 FY27. On a sequential basis, profit rose 16% from Rs 82 crore in the preceding quarter (Q4 FY26).
At the close of trading on Wednesday, Kissht's shares were priced at Rs 343.45, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 5,796 crore ($610 million).

title: TBO Tek’s Q1 FY27 revenue jumps 81% to Rs 926 Cr; profit grows 32%
summary:
Travel distribution platform TBO Tek reported an 81.2% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue for the first quarter of FY27, while its profit increased 31.7% during the same period.
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 926 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 511 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).


 
Hotel and package bookings remained TBO Tek’s largest revenue stream, contributing Rs 800 crore in Q1 FY27, up 89.1% from Rs 423 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from air ticketing increased marginally to Rs 81 crore from Rs 78 crore, while other operating revenue climbed to Rs 45 crore from Rs 10.4 crore.
Including Rs 13 crore in other income, the company’s total income stood at Rs 939 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 524 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a sequential basis, operating revenue grew 13.8% from Rs 814 crore in Q4 FY26.
On the expense front, service fees remained the largest cost component, rising to Rs 373 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 179 crore, while depreciation and finance costs stood at Rs 33 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively.
Overall expenditure grew 83.1% to Rs 835 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 456 crore in Q1 FY26.
Despite higher expenses, TBO Tek’s profit increased to Rs 83 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 63 crore in Q1 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit rose 38.3% from Rs 60 crore in Q4 FY26.
TBO Tek’s share price closed at Rs 1,522.60, with a total market capitalization of Rs 16,385 crore.

summary:
IPO-bound B2B commerce and financing platform OfBusiness reported a 21% year-on-year growth in its profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 724 crore in FY26 from Rs 597 crore in the previous fiscal, while its consolidated revenue stood at Rs 20,645 crore.
The company's commerce business, which spans metals, chemicals, apparel and food processing, recorded a revenue of Rs 19,174 crore during the fiscal year. Its EBITDA grew 34% to Rs 769 crore in FY26 from Rs 575 crore in FY25, while EBITDA margin expanded to 4% from 2.6% a year ago.
OfBusiness also reported a sharp improvement in cash generation, with operating cash flow from its commerce business rising to Rs 1,302 crore in FY26 from Rs 715 crore in the previous fiscal. The company turned free cash flow to firm (FCFF) positive for the first time, reporting Rs 390 crore during the year.
Its financing arm, Oxyzo Financial Services, reported an asset base of Rs 11,800 crore in FY26, 28% higher than the previous fiscal. The lending business posted a return on assets of 3.8% and maintained a gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio of 0.75%.
Founded in 2015 by Asish Mohapatra, Ruchi Kalra, Bhuvan Gupta and Vasant Sridhar, OfBusiness operates a technology-led platform that offers SMEs raw material procurement, working capital financing, and tender intelligence solutions. 
Its tender intelligence platform, BidAssist, has crossed 1.5 million business users and aggregates over 50,000 live tenders daily from authorities and portals across India. The platform uses AI to match tenders with business profiles, helps users track win rates and competitors in live bids, and serves as a customer acquisition channel for OfBusiness's commerce and financing businesses.
The company's workforce has also crossed 30,000 employees, nearly doubling over the past year, led by the expansion of its apparel business in South India.
Commenting on the performance, co-founder and CEO Asish Mohapatra said, “The year saw the Group crossing significant milestones, becoming free cash flow to firm positive in the Commerce business and crossing the Rs 10,000 crore AuM mark in lending. FY27 will be a pivotal year for us as returns from prior investments play out.”

title: CarTrade reports Rs 201 Cr revenue and Rs 57 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
summary:
Automobile classifieds platform CarTrade announced its financial results for the first quarter of FY27 on Wednesday, reporting over 16% year-on-year growth in its revenue from operations. The company's profit also increased 21% to Rs 57 crore during the quarter.
CarTrade’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 201 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 173 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The Mumbai-based company operates across three key segments: Consumer, Remarketing, and Classifieds. The Consumer segment remained the largest contributor, with Rs 78 crore in revenue during Q1 FY27, followed by Remarketing at Rs 67 crore and Classifieds at Rs 62 crore, before Rs 6.4 crore in intersegment eliminations.
Besides its core operations, CarTrade recorded Rs 29 crore in non-operating income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 230 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 199 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a quarterly basis, its operating revenue declined marginally from Rs 203 crore in the previous quarter (Q4 FY26).
On the cost side, employee benefits remained the largest expense, accounting for nearly 55% of the company’s total expenditure. This cost increased to Rs 83 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 75 crore in Q1 FY26. Other expenses stood at Rs 55 crore, while depreciation and finance costs were Rs 11 crore and Rs 3.2 crore, respectively.
CarTrade’s overall expenditure increased 7% to Rs 152 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 142 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.
Growth across its operating segments, coupled with a relatively controlled increase in expenditure, helped CarTrade's profit rise 21.3% to Rs 57 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 47 crore in Q1 FY26. On a sequential basis, however, its profit declined nearly 20% from Rs 71 crore in Q4 FY26.
According to a separate exchange filing, CarTrade Tech has partnered with Spinny to strengthen the used-car buying and selling experience across CarWale and OLX India. Through the collaboration, users will be able to access Spinny's quality-assured used-car offerings, while CarTrade will leverage its proprietary VAYA AI technology to connect consumers with relevant listings in real time.
CarTrade’s share price is currently trading at Rs 2,812 (as of 11:32 AM), with a total market capitalization of Rs 14,187 crore.

title: Ferns N Petals plans 2028 IPO as it eyes 25% annual growth
summary:
Ferns N Petals (FNP), an omni-channel gifting and floral retail company, is planning to go public by the end of 2028 as it looks to accelerate its expansion plans and pursue acquisitions, according to Reuters.
The Lighthouse-backed company is targeting an annual revenue growth of around 25% over the next few years, Global CEO Pawan Gadia told Reuters. The IPO proceeds will be deployed towards expanding its business and acquiring brands in the gifting space.
FNP reported a revenue of Rs 1,085 crore in FY26, reflecting a 25% year-on-year growth. The company is also sharpening its focus on profitability and expects its core earnings margin to improve to 5–6% this fiscal from 2.5% in the previous year.
Founded in 1994, Ferns N Petals (FNP) is an omnichannel gifting platform that sells flowers, cakes, and personalized gifts through its website, third-party e-commerce marketplaces, company-owned stores, and franchise outlets.
FNP operates across India, the UAE, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar, with India contributing nearly 55% of its revenue, and plans to expand into Malaysia and additional Gulf markets.
As part of its expansion strategy, the company plans to increase its retail footprint to 350 stores by FY28 from around 280 currently. While the brand will continue opening company-owned stores in metro cities, it plans to adopt a franchise-led model in smaller towns.
FNP has raised around $27 million in funding to date, with Lighthouse among its key investors. Beyond its gifting business, the company also operates hospitality and wedding ventures under Udman Hotels and FNP Weddings and Events. It competes with players such as IGP (Indian Gifts Portal), FlowerAura, Winni, and Archies.

title: Building materials quick commerce startup Fixxly raises $5.5 Mn in seed round
summary:
Bengaluru-based building materials quick commerce startup Fixxly has raised $5.5 million in a seed funding round from Accel, Fireside Ventures and Lightspeed India Partners.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its technology platform and scale operations ahead of its commercial launch on September 1. It will begin operations in Bengaluru before expanding to other cities.
Founded in 2026 by Shezan Bhojani and Sachith Varma, Fixxly is building an AI-powered quick commerce platform for building materials. The platform enables contractors, electricians, plumbers, carpenters, painters, interior designers and homeowners to order products such as plywood, paint, electricals, lighting, hardware and plumbing supplies, with deliveries in as little as 30 minutes.
The startup operates an AI-powered supply network that fulfils orders through a network of local dark stores, matching real-time inventory, proximity and demand.
Before launching Fixxly, Bhojani co-founded home interiors startup DesignCafe, which merged with HomeLane in 2024. His cofounder, Sachith Varma, previously led supply chain design at Zepto and managed last-mile operations at Flipkart.

title: Piper Serica leads Rs 15 Cr seed round in deep tech startup Yaanendriya
summary:
Yaanendriya, a Bengaluru-based deep tech company building indigenous sensor, navigation, and control technologies for mobile robots and critical applications, has raised Rs 15 crore in a seed funding round led by Piper Serica.
The fresh funds will be used to strengthen research and development, accelerate product development, and expand its portfolio of high precision navigation systems for mission critical environments, Yaanendriya said in a press release.
Co-founded in February last year by Vamshi Bharadwaj M V, Vyshak Y, Vijay HP, and Aravind Thumbur, Yaanendriya develops indigenous sensor, navigation, and control technologies for robotics, aerospace, and other critical applications.
Its portfolio includes the SynCore series of navigation controllers for autonomous robotic platforms and the YDX series of high precision inertial sensors deployed across commercial applications globally. The company is also developing navigation systems and a hardware agnostic platform for space and other critical missions, along with high precision MEMS inertial sensors for the NewSpace sector.
Yaanendriya builds sensor and control platforms that enable autonomous systems, including drones, ground robots, spacecraft, and underwater vehicles, to sense motion, estimate their state, and maintain control in environments where GNSS is unavailable, unreliable, or intentionally disrupted.
Its SynCore navigation controllers combine inputs from multiple sensors to estimate orientation, position, and velocity while supporting real time stabilization and control. The platform is deployed by robotics companies across aerial, ground, and underwater applications in sectors such as defence, surveillance, and agriculture.
The company's YDX series of high precision inertial sensors is deployed across four continents in applications including motion capture for gaming, unmanned vehicles, and surgical robots.

title: Pine Labs reports  Rs 737 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps over 4X
summary:
Pine Labs reports  Rs 737 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps over 4X  
Fintech major Pine Labs has announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 20% year-on-year growth in operating scale, while its profits jumped 4X to Rs 20 crore during the period.
Pine Labs’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 737 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 616 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Revenue from its digital infrastructure and transaction platform was the largest contributor, which grew 14.9% to Rs 499.12 crore in Q1 FY27. Its issuing and acquiring platform grew by 31% to Rs 237.8 crore during the same period.
The company added Rs 29 crore from non-operating activities, taking its total income to Rs 766 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 653 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a sequential basis, the Bengaluru-based firm’s revenue increased marginally by 5% compared to Rs 701 crore in Q4 FY26.
Employee benefits remained the largest cost centre for Pine Labs, accounting for 36.8% of its overall expenditure. Interestingly, this cost declined 7.9% to Rs 268 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 291 crore in Q1 FY26.
The cost of materials consumed increased 39% to Rs 107 crore, while transaction and related costs surged 61.7% to Rs 97 crore. Depreciation rose 12.3% to Rs 73 crore, whereas other expenses increased 10.9% to Rs 183 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenditure increased 10.6% to Rs 728 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 658 crore in Q1 FY26.
The faster growth in revenue compared to expenses helped Pine Labs to zoom its profit by fourfold to Rs 20 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 5 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a unit level, Pine Labs spent Rs 0.99 to earn a rupee of operating revenue during Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 1.07 in the year-ago quarter.
At 3:05 PM, Pine Labs’ shares were trading at Rs 151 apiece, taking its market capitalization to Rs 17,188 crore.

title: UpGrad set to close Unacademy acquisition in three weeks; deal valued at Rs 1,955 Cr
summary:
The acquisition of edtech platform Unacademy by upGrad has entered its final phase, with the transaction expected to close within the next three weeks, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Sources said that almost all institutional investors have signed the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA), while all angel investors have signed the Share Purchase Agreement (SPA), which leaves only the final formalities before the deal is completed.
According to sources, the all-stock transaction has been pegged at around Rs 1,955 crore. The current deal is slightly lower than the valuation discussed when the deal was announced earlier this year.
As part of the transaction, Unacademy co-founder Gaurav Munjal will continue as the company's CEO after the merger. Meanwhile, language learning platform Airlearn, which was incubated within Unacademy, is also part of the acquisition and will move under the upGrad umbrella.
Following the acquisition, upGrad is also consolidating the operations of Unacademy and its businesses. PrepLadder's headquarters has already been shifted from Chandigarh to Bengaluru, and Unacademy, PrepLadder, Airlearn and Graphy will operate from Bengaluru going forward.
In another key development, Unacademy's existing investors will receive one board seat in upGrad after the transaction is completed, according to sources.
Entrackr has reached out to Unacademy and upGrad for comments. 
The acquisition, first announced earlier this year, marks one of the biggest consolidation moves in India's edtech sector. The transaction received regulatory clearance from the Competition Commission of India (CCI) earlier this month, paving the way for its completion. Once closed, the combined entity will bring together upGrad's higher education and upskilling business with Unacademy's test preparation, medical education and creator-led learning platforms.
Financially, the two companies have taken different paths. Unacademy's operating revenue declined 16% year-on-year to Rs 826.3 crore in FY25, while upGrad reported a provisional profit of Rs 38.8 crore during the 11 months ended February 2026, turning EBITDA positive with Rs 56.9 crore on operating revenue of Rs 1,531.7 crore.

title: BigBasket's B2C arm losses cross Rs 3,000 Cr in FY26
summary:
The battle for India's online grocery market has become more intense as platforms chase scale, speed, and profitability. While demand remains strong, profitability continues to remain elusive for most players. Against this backdrop, BigBasket posted marginal growth in FY26 with its operating revenue crossing Rs 8,000 crore, even as its core B2C business continued to bleed. The Tata Digital-backed firm's performance mirrors broader sector trends, where grocery delivery platforms continue to post heavy losses despite rapid expansion.
According to Tata Sons' FY26 annual report, Innovative Retail Concepts, which operates BigBasket's consumer-facing business, recorded a 7.7% increase in turnover to Rs 8,223 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,634 crore in the previous fiscal year. However, its losses widened 66% to Rs 3,073 crore from Rs 1,850 crore during the same period.

BigBasket's losses have risen sharply since its complete pivot to quick commerce in August 2024. The shift has raised operating costs as the company spends more on logistics, dark stores, discounts, and customer retention to compete in the rapidly expanding segment.
Meanwhile, BigBasket's B2B arm, Supermarket Grocery Supplies, which handles procurement and backend operations, reported flat revenue of Rs 2,298 crore in FY26, while its losses remained unchanged at Rs 102 crore during the fiscal year.
Together, the two entities reported Rs 10,521 crore in revenue in FY26, compared to Rs 9,861 crore in the previous fiscal year. Their combined losses stood at Rs 3,175 crore during the year.
Tata Digital, which acquired a majority stake in BigBasket in 2021, remains its largest shareholder with an 84.23% stake.
BigBasket's rival Zepto reported Rs 22,624 crore in revenue and a loss of Rs 5,905 crore in FY26, while quick commerce leader Blinkit posted Rs 15,664 crore in revenue and a positive adjusted EBITDA of Rs 102 crore in Q1 FY27.
At the group level, Tata Digital reported a 12% increase in revenue to Rs 35,990 crore in FY26 from Rs 32,188 crore in FY25. However, its net loss widened to Rs 4,974 crore from Rs 4,610 crore during the same period. The company's gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at Rs 46,515 crore in FY26.

title: Instamart appoints former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha as CEO; Amitesh Jha resigns
summary:
Swiggy's quick commerce arm Instamart has appointed former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha as its Chief Executive Officer, effective August 3. 
Sinha succeeds Amitesh Jha, who has resigned to pursue other opportunities. Jha joined Instamart as CEO in August 2024 after leaving Flipkart.
The appointment was announced on Tuesday by Swiggy, which said Jha had tendered his resignation on July 28 and would cease to be part of the company's senior management personnel from August 3.
"Nandita is one of India's most accomplished consumer internet leaders, and I'm enthusiastic about the vision, customer obsession and operational rigor she brings to the team we've built at Instamart," said Sriharsha Majety, Managing Director and Group CEO of Swiggy.
Majety also credited Jha for leading Instamart through a key phase of expansion, highlighting initiatives such as the launch of Noice and improvements in the platform's contribution margins.
Sinha joins Instamart after serving as CEO of Myntra, where she led the fashion ecommerce platform through a period of market share gains and EBITDA profitability. She brings more than two decades of experience across consumer internet, ecommerce and FMCG, having previously held leadership roles at Flipkart, Britannia and Hindustan Unilever.
She will oversee Instamart's next phase of growth, with a focus on expanding its assortment strategy, improving profitability, strengthening customer experience and driving operational excellence.
This is the third senior-level exit at Instamart in recent months, following the departures of chief operating officer (COO) Ankit Jain and chief business officer (CBO) Hari Kumar. On Tuesday, Jain joined listed beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa to lead its quick commerce vertical, Nykaa Now.

The fund is anchored by the Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund, HDFC Asset Management Company and HDFC AMC Select AIF FoF, with participation from international institutional investors.
Fund III will invest in science, engineering and technology startups at the pre-Series A and Series A stages. The firm plans to write initial cheques of Rs 15–45 crore and build a portfolio of 22–25 companies.
According to Inflexor Ventures, the new fund will place greater emphasis on Series A investments while continuing its sector-agnostic approach focused on technology-driven businesses with high barriers to entry.
Fund III has already begun deploying capital and expects to announce its first investments in the coming weeks.
Founded by Venkat Vallabhaneni, Jatin Desai and Pratip Mazumdar, Inflexor Ventures manages around Rs 1,300 crore in assets and has backed more than 25 startups, including Atomberg, Bellatrix Aerospace, CloudSEK, CredFlow, Kale Logistics and PlayShifu.

title: Tata 1mg revenue nears Rs 3,000 Cr in FY26; loss narrows to Rs 287 Cr
summary:
Tata 1mg, the digital healthcare platform backed by Tata Digital, continued its growth momentum in FY26, with revenue nearing the Rs 3,000 crore mark while reducing its losses during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Tata 1mg’s consolidated revenue grew 23% to Rs 2,936 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,392 crore in FY25, according to Tata Sons’ annual report.
Tata 1mg is a healthtech platform that enables users to order allopathic, ayurvedic, and homeopathic medicines, vitamins, nutrition supplements, and other healthcare products online. The platform also offers diagnostics and other healthcare services.
The company’s revenue came from two entities: Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions Private Limited, which contributed Rs 2,440 crore, and Tata 1mg Technologies Private Limited, which added Rs 496 crore. Together, the two entities generated Rs 2,936 crore in revenue during FY26.
On the bottom line, Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions reported a loss of Rs 310 crore, while Tata 1mg Technologies remained profitable with a net profit of Rs 23 crore. On a combined basis, Tata 1mg posted a net loss of Rs 287 crore in FY26.
On the balance sheet, the combined Tata 1mg entities had total assets of Rs 2,268 crore at the end of FY26. Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions accounted for Rs 805 crore, while Tata 1mg Technologies held assets worth Rs 1,463 crore.

title: Delhi HC halts Unity SFB’s share capital plan in BharatPe dispute
summary:

According to court proceedings, the bank had proposed increasing its authorised share capital from Rs 4,000 crore to Rs 4,900 crore. The proposal was aimed at facilitating the conversion of certain warrants into compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) before their expiry later this year.
BharatPe opposed the move and argued that the proposal could not be carried out without its consent under the shareholders' agreement. The fintech company also claimed that the conversion would significantly dilute its stake in Unity SFB.
The High Court has directed the bank not to place the proposal before its board for now, while the dispute is being resolved through arbitration. The order is interim in nature and does not decide the merits of the case.
The dispute marks the latest chapter in the evolving relationship between BharatPe and Centrum Group, the two key shareholders of Unity SFB.
Unity Small Finance Bank was launched in 2021 after a consortium led by BharatPe and Centrum Financial Services took over the troubled Punjab and Maharashtra Cooperative (PMC) Bank under a Reserve Bank of India-backed reconstruction scheme. BharatPe initially emerged as one of the largest shareholders in the bank, with a stake close to 49%.
However, differences have surfaced between the shareholders over governance and capital-related decisions. BharatPe has alleged that the proposed capital restructuring would materially reduce its ownership without the approvals required under the shareholder agreement.
The case is significant as it highlights the importance of shareholder rights and governance in financial institutions, particularly those created under regulatory reconstruction plans. The arbitration proceedings will now determine whether the proposed capital increase and share conversion comply with the agreements signed between the parties.

Employee benefits expenses rose modestly by 9% to Rs 47 crore, which notably included Rs 7 crore in non-cash ESOP costs. Other overheads like delivery and handling charges, rent, IT, legal & professional expenses pushed overall expenses for Bombay Shaving Company parent by 98% to Rs 650 crore in FY25 from Rs 329 crore in FY25.
The Gurugram-based Company managed to reduce its net loss by 85% to Rs 9 crore in FY26 from Rs 58 crore in FY25. Notably, the firm posted an adjusted EBITDA (net of ESOP cost) of Rs 2 crore during FY26. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at -5.2% and -0.79%, respectively. On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.02 to earn a rupee in FY26.

title: CBDT issues operational clarity on crypto reporting, exchanges to collect tax residency details
summary:
The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued a detailed guidance note clarifying how crypto exchanges and other virtual digital asset (VDA) service providers should comply with India's new crypto reporting framework under the Income-tax Rules, 2026.
The guidance provides operational clarity on the recently introduced reporting requirements and aligns India's framework with the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).
Under the new framework, crypto exchanges and other Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Providers (RCASPs) will be required to collect additional information from users, including their tax residency status and Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), wherever applicable. The entities will also have to maintain detailed transaction records and submit annual reports to the Income Tax Department.
The guidance further explains how exchanges should identify reportable users, determine the account holder in different scenarios, and handle cross-border transactions where more than one jurisdiction may have reporting obligations. It also distinguishes between crypto-assets, central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), and specified electronic money products for reporting purposes.
The clarification is expected to help crypto exchanges prepare their compliance systems before the reporting rules come into effect. Market participants will need to strengthen their KYC and record-keeping processes to meet the new requirements.
While the guidance does not introduce any new tax on virtual digital assets, it lays down the operational framework for reporting crypto transactions and sharing information with tax authorities.
For India's crypto industry, the latest guidance marks another step towards a more regulated environment. Exchanges will now need to invest in compliance infrastructure and ensure that customer onboarding and reporting processes are aligned with the CBDT's expectations under the new regime.

title: Decoding PhonePe FY26: The Rs 364 Cr loss behind the Rs 2,792 Cr headline
summary:
Walmart-backed fintech PhonePe reported modest growth in FY26, but its reported loss of Rs 2,792 crore doesn't tell the complete story. A closer look at the company's financial statements shows that a significant part of the loss came from non-cash accounting adjustments instead of its core ops.
Let's first look at where PhonePe's revenue came from.
The company reported operating revenue of Rs 7,920 crore in FY26. The bulk of this came from payment services, including transaction processing fees from bill payments, digital gold, and travel bookings. It also earned from platform fees, subscription fees for payment devices and smart speakers, advertising income, and its financial services businesses such as insurance, lending, stock broking, and mutual fund distribution. Together, these businesses contributed Rs 7,619 crore during the year.
In addition, PhonePe received Rs 286 crore as incentives from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Interest income and other non-operating gains pushed its total income to Rs 8,388 crore in FY26.
On the expense side, employee benefits remained the largest cost at Rs 4,386 crore. However, only Rs 1,994 crore, or around 45%, was paid as salaries. The remaining Rs 2,390 crore was booked as ESOP (employee stock option) expense.
Notably, around Rs 2,197 crore, or 91% of the ESOP expense, was a non-cash accounting charge. Since this does not involve an actual cash outflow, we have excluded it to understand the company's underlying operating performance.
Payment processing charges stood at Rs 1,907 crore during the year. Meanwhile, advertising and sales promotion expenses nearly doubled to Rs 956 crore. Including technology infrastructure, licensing fees, customer support, legal, logistics, and other administrative expenses, the company's total expenditure reached Rs 10,589 crore in FY26.
PhonePe also reported an exceptional loss of Rs 231 crore, largely due to goodwill impairment. Since this is another non-cash accounting adjustment and not related to regular operations, it has also been excluded from our adjusted loss calculation.
As a result, while PhonePe reported a net loss of Rs 2,792 crore in FY26, excluding the non-cash ESOP expense of Rs 2,197 crore and the exceptional goodwill impairment of Rs 231 crore brings the adjusted loss down to around Rs 364 crore.
The company also reported a loss of Rs 364 crore from its discontinued operations, mainly related to the closure of its hyperlocal commerce business, Pincode. Since the business generated limited revenue and has now been shut down, this move could help improve PhonePe's profitability going forward by eliminating a loss-making vertical.
Operationally, PhonePe continued to dominate India's UPI ecosystem. In June, it processed 10.48 billion UPI transactions, marking the fourth consecutive month in which it handled more than 10 billion transactions. The company accounted for 46.15% of total UPI transaction volume and 49.07% of transaction value, processing payments worth Rs 14.19 lakh crore during the month.
Earlier this year, PhonePe filed updated draft papers with SEBI for its proposed IPO, which is expected to raise around Rs 12,000 crore (approximately $1.5 billion). However, the Walmart-backed company has temporarily paused its listing plans amid geopolitical uncertainty and volatility in global financial markets.

title: WhatsApp overtakes CRED in UPI volume in June; PhonePe retains lead
summary:
WhatsApp overtook CRED in Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transaction volume in June, processing 150.48 million transactions compared with CRED's 141.78 million, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The crossover comes in the same month that CRED founder Kunal Shah stepped down from the fintech firm to take over as the global CEO of WhatsApp. Miten Sampat was named interim CEO of CRED following Shah's move.
In May, CRED had processed 157 million UPI transactions, ahead of WhatsApp's more than 150 million transactions.
Despite its lower transaction volume in June, CRED processed transactions worth Rs 55,117 crore and accounted for 1.91% of UPI transaction value. WhatsApp's transaction value stood at Rs 11,392 crore, translating to a 0.39% share.
Meanwhile, Walmart-backed digital payments platform PhonePe retained its dominance in the UPI ecosystem with 10.48 billion transactions in June, compared with 10.73 billion in May.
This was the fourth consecutive month that PhonePe processed more than 10 billion UPI transactions. The platform first crossed the 10 billion monthly transaction milestone in March 2026.

UPI recorded 22.72 billion transactions during June, compared with 23.2 billion transactions in May. The total transaction value declined to Rs 28.92 lakh crore from Rs 29.90 lakh crore in the previous month.
PhonePe accounted for 46.15% of total UPI transaction volume in June. In value terms, the platform held a 49.07% share after processing transactions worth Rs 14.19 lakh crore.
Google Pay retained the second spot with 7.41 billion transactions during June, translating to a 32.61% market share by volume. By value, its share stood at 33.44% after transactions worth Rs 9.67 lakh crore.
Paytm remained the third-largest UPI player with 1.80 billion transactions. The fintech major captured 7.92% market share by volume and 6.66% by value, with transactions worth Rs 1.93 lakh crore.
Among other players, Navi recorded 842.51 million transactions in June, up from more than 824 million in May, and captured a 3.71% share by volume. Flipkart-backed super.money processed 430.24 million transactions, while BHIM registered 223.54 million transactions during the month.
FamApp by Trio recorded 195.31 million transactions during the month, while Axis Bank's apps contributed 136.16 million transactions across customer-initiated, B2C, and B2B payments.
PhonePe and Google Pay together accounted for 78.76% of UPI transaction volume and 82.51% of transaction value during June. The two platforms continued to remain far ahead of other players in the country's UPI ecosystem.

title: Pronto widens AI camera rollout in homes with ‘Verified’ offering
summary:
Home services platform Pronto has confirmed that it is continuing and expanding the use of wearable cameras inside customers' homes through Pronto Verified, an opt in service that records service sessions and uses anonymized footage for AI training.
The confirmation comes nearly two months after Entrackr first reported in May that Pronto was piloting a Physical AI initiative involving AI enabled wearable cameras inside customers' homes to collect real world data for AI models. At the time, the company had described the initiative as a pilot on a small fraction of bookings.
Following Entrackr's report, peers Snabbit and Urban Company publicly said they were not pursuing similar initiatives involving wearable cameras inside customers' homes.
Responding to Entrackr's latest questionnaire, Pronto said the initiative has now evolved into Pronto Verified, which it described as an optional service.
"The camera is a recording device, and its only on device intelligence is encryption. But yes, we're scaling Pronto Verified."
According to the company, customers opt into Verified bookings, which create "a record of the work" for customers while allowing professionals to earn materially more. The company said professionals currently earn about double for every Verified booking.
Customers opt in, anonymized footage used for AI training
Pronto confirmed that anonymized footage captured during Verified bookings is used to train its AI models.
According to the company, customers are informed that recordings may be used for AI training before making a Verified booking. It said customers provide consent multiple times during the booking process and once again when the professional arrives.
The company also said customers can decline recording at any point and proceed with a standard Pronto booking instead.
"We use the anonymized footage for AI training and this is disclosed in our terms and conditions."
Data handling and privacy
Pronto said the wearable camera records video but does not capture audio.
According to the company, raw footage is encrypted, automatically deleted immediately after the work is completed, and is never accessed by humans. It said only an anonymized version, where faces and personally identifiable information have been blurred or removed, is retained.
Customers can review the anonymized recording within 48 hours of the session, after which the anonymized footage is used for AI training, the company said.
On concerns around children, family members, domestic staff or visitors who may appear in recordings, Pronto said customers are asked during booking to confirm they are consenting on behalf of everyone in the home. It also said the camera points down at the professional's work area, hands and forearms, and aims to capture nothing else.
Company on regulatory engagement
Asked whether the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) or any other regulator sought an explanation after the May controversy, Pronto did not directly answer the question.
Instead, the company said it has had "encouraging engagement with all stakeholders" and said much of the discussion in May stemmed from "a misunderstanding of how the program worked," particularly around customer disclosures. It added that disclosures have since been strengthened and are now explicit at multiple stages for participants.
Founder details ‘Pronto verified’
On Friday, after Entrackr sent its questionnaire, Pronto founder Anjali Sardana published a LinkedIn post outlining the company's approach to Pronto Verified.
In the post, Sardana said the company is "scaling Verified" and described it as an opt in booking where customers choose to have work recorded. She said professionals wear a camera that records only the work activity, customers pay a premium for the service, and professionals are paid about double compared with standard bookings.
She also reiterated that customers are informed that recordings may be used for AI training, consent is obtained at multiple stages, the camera does not capture audio, raw footage is deleted immediately after the session, and only anonymized data is retained for AI training.

title: Fractal reports Rs 72 Cr profit on Rs 913 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27
summary:
AI and advanced analytics firm Fractal has announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 20% year on year increase in revenue, crossing the Rs 900 crore mark, while its profit surged 90% to Rs 72 crore during the period.
Fractal’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 913 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 761 crore in Q1 FY26, according to disclosures sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Founded in 2000, Fractal earns revenue from analytics and consulting services, as well as licensing and subscription fees from its AI platforms, including Cogentiq, fflyfish.ai, and Kalaido.ai.
The firm also generated Rs 20 crore from non operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 932 crore during the quarter.
Employee benefit expenses, the company’s largest cost component, accounted for more than 77% of total spending and grew 14% year-on-year to Rs 632 crore in Q1 FY27. Higher depreciation, finance costs, and other overheads drove total expenses up 17% to Rs 818 crore during the quarter from Rs 700 crore in Q1 FY26.
As revenue grew at a slightly faster pace than expenses, Fractal reported a 90% year-on-year jump in profit to Rs 72 crore in the first quarter of FY27 from Rs 38 crore a year ago. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, however, profit declined 38% from Rs 116 crore recorded in Q4 FY26.
Fractal went public in February this year through a Rs 2,834 crore IPO, comprising both a fresh issue and an offer for sale. The public offering provided exits to existing investors, including Apax Partners and TPG Capital. The stock debuted at a 3% discount to its issue price.At the end of Thursday’s trading session, Fractal’s share price closed at Rs 866, with a total market capitalization of Rs 14,892 crore ($1.56 billion).

title: Go Digit reports 38% decline in Q1 FY27 profit as claims surge
summary:
Go Digit General Insurance reported a 7.6% year-on-year increase in its net premium during Q1 FY27. However, its profit declined 37.7% during the same period.
The company's net premium rose to Rs 2,007 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,865 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its regulatory filings.
Meanwhile, gross premium fell 8.4% to Rs 2,731 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,982 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, as per its quarterly results filed with the NSE.
Motor insurance continued to be Go Digit's largest business segment, contributing Rs 1,510 crore in premium, followed by health insurance at Rs 366 crore. The company also generated premium from fire, corporate, marine, crop, and other insurance segments.
Income from investments increased to Rs 352 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 314 crore in the year-ago quarter. Supported by gains from its investment portfolio and other non-operating income, the company's total income grew to Rs 2,359 crore during the quarter.
On the expense side, commission and brokerage costs rose to Rs 615 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 572 crore in Q1 FY26. Employee benefit expenses increased 10% to Rs 99 crore from Rs 90 crore a year earlier.
Claims paid surged 16% to Rs 1,046 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 902 crore in the same quarter last year. As a result, total expenses rose 11.2% to Rs 2,289 crore from Rs 2,058 crore.
The increase in claims and operating expenses weighed on the company's profitability, with net profit declining 37.7% to Rs 86 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 138 crore in Q1 FY26.
Go Digit's shares closed at Rs 283 per share at the end of Thursday's trading session, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 26,166 crore (around $2.7 billion).

title: Exclusive: Urban Harvest board to approve Rs 341 Cr Series D round from 58 investors
summary:
B2B food-tech startup Urban Harvest is set to raise Rs 341.4 crore or $35.9 million in a Series D round led by Info Edge, with participation from Sandeep Kapadia, J & A Partners, and several other investors.
The board at Urban Harvest will consider approving the issuance of 42,013 Series D compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 81,260 each to raise the capital, according to its regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.
The round will be led by Info Edge, with an investment of Rs 30 crore, followed by Sandeep Kapadia and J & A Partners, which will invest Rs 27 crore and Rs 25 crore, respectively. Renu Sehgal Trust and Lc Nueva Advisors will contribute Rs 20.01 crore each.
Other notable investors include Saburi Projects LLP at Rs 15 crore, Madhuri Madhusudan Kela at Rs 13.09 crore, and Viral Amal Parikh at Rs 11.56 crore. Gauri Khan Family Trust, will also participate with Rs 5.01 crore. Several other individual and institutional investors will contribute the remaining capital, taking the total number of investors in the round to 58.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, Urban Harvest will be valued at around Rs 1,541 crore or $162 million following the Series D round. The company plans to use the fresh proceeds to fund its business expansion and growth, meet working capital requirements, support marketing initiatives, and for general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2019, Urban Harvest is a B2B food-tech platform that supplies fresh produce, food ingredients, and automated coffee machines to restaurants and cloud kitchens. The company operates a quick-commerce model focused on the HoReCa segment and currently serves around 16,000 restaurants every month across multiple cities.
Urban Harvest operates five dark warehouses across four cities and plans to add five more as it expands into new markets. The company also owns packaged water brand Hello Fresh and acquired gourmet food brand Cocosutra for Rs 2.5 crore in an all-cash deal.

Following the allotment of the Series D round, Info Edge will hold an 18.83% stake, followed by Sandeep Kapadia at 5.01%, Madhuri Madhusudan Kela at 4.25%, Viral Amal Parikh at 3.75%, and J & A Partners at 3.12%.

Mint had earlier reported that Urban Urban Harvest in talks to raise Rs 300 crore
According to the report, Urban Harvest’s revenue surged to Rs 385 crore in FY26 from Rs 118 crore in FY25, while it posted a profit of Rs 3.5 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 35 lakh in the previous fiscal year.
